messages:
mia: Quick weekly check-in for Acme — noticed an uptick in failures this week, primarily 5xx + timeouts. Sharing a short breakdown and top failing endpoints. We should decide short-term mitigations and an enablement outreach.

carmen: Can you drop the raw counts? :eyes:

mia: Here are the aggregated failure counts for the last 7 days (UTC):
```
Total failures: 897
- 5xx: 412 (46%)
- timeouts: 310 (34%)
- rate_limit: 175 (20%)

Top failing endpoints by failure count:
1) POST /v1/generate (backend handler: gen-service) — 342 failures (mostly 5xx + timeouts)
2) POST /v1/embeddings (batching proxy: embed-proxy) — 210 failures (timeouts + rate_limit)
3) POST /v1/chat/stream (streaming-edge) — 155 failures (partial frames -> 5xx)
4) POST /v1/rerank (reranker) — 90 failures (mostly 5xx)
5) GET /v1/status (health checks) — 100 failures (timeouts)

Spike window: 2026-03-14 01:10 -> 2026-03-14 03:45 UTC
Peak queue depth: GPU pool-21 at 87% (normal 45-60%)
Median request size for failures: ~1.2k tokens
```

ops-bot: Deploy to prod completed by @ravi at 2026-03-14T00:58:12Z — commit 4f3a9c. No rollbacks recorded.

ravi: I didn't change routing rules in that deploy. Looking at pool metrics now; we had a sudden traffic burst, queueing caused increased latency and timeouts.

jordan: Are these correlated with Acme's onboarding batch jobs (long prompts + large embedding batches)?

mia: Yes — 57% of failing requests were from their new onboarding flow (long prompt generation) and 28% from bulk embedding batches. Their client started sending larger-than-usual batch sizes on 2026-03-13.

carmen: Short-term mitigations I recommend:
- Increase server-side request timeout for Acme routes from `30s` -> `60s` (reduce timeouts while we stabilize)
- Apply soft throttling for embedding batches (> 64 items) via rate-limit policy for their API key
- Canary traffic to model-variant `gpt-redwood-v1.2-quant` for 5% of requests to rule out model regressions
- Temporarily raise dedicated concurrency on Acme's Dedicated pool by +20% if capacity allows

ravi: I'll apply the timeout bump and add a rate-limit rule for their key. Will start canary for 5% now and report results in ~15m.

mia: Thanks. Also flagging as a potential renewal risk if we can't stabilize within 48h — customer success to coordinate enablement material for their engineers.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-87 (P2) — assigned to eng-oncall.

carmen: Follow-up items: create a small targeted eval set from Acme's prompt examples to run against canary variant and baseline. I'll own the eval and email results to the account team.

jordan: I'll reach out to Acme PM to confirm recent onboarding changes and share mitigation plan.

mia: Great. Please update this thread when the canary completes and when rate-limit rule is live. Also attaching a short customer-facing blurb for enablement: 

```
Short note for Acme engineers:
- We observed spikes due to large prompt generations and embedding batch sizes.
- We're increasing server timeouts and applying temporary throttles on very large embedding batches.
- Expected impact: reduced timeouts within 10-30 minutes; minor throughput degradation for very large batch requests.
- If you need faster throughput for bulk embeddings, please let us know and we can schedule a tuned dedicated window.
```

mia: ping @ravi for canary results.

ravi: Canary started at 2026-03-14T02:05:00Z — initial 500 requests routed. Error rate reduced by ~35% on canary variant (prelim). Will run extended 5k request sample.

mia: Good progress — keep the account team posted.
